text:
incident-bot: PAGING — Dedicated pool ded-acme-eu-1: sustained 5xx spike (4.8% errors) starting 2026-03-15T08:15Z. Affected: AcmePay production. Pager: @maria. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-errors
maria: On it. Checking queue and GPU metrics now.
maria: queue depth gpu-queue-3 = 620 (baseline ~40), 95th latency up to 1.2s, tokens/sec falling. Correlated with a sudden traffic surge from AcmePay.
kevin: seeing same in grafana. Logs show repeated OOM/retry loops for model rwd/gpt-large-8k on that pool.
oliver: if it's a traffic surge, we can either increase burst capacity or apply per-customer rate limiting. Which do we prefer short-term?
maria: short-term: bump burst capacity and enable a soft quota for AcmePay route. Proposed plan:
1) increase pool burst capacity +2 instances
2) enable route throttle for AcmePay to 200 rps
3) disable feature flag ff.dynamic_system_prompts for AcmePay (suspected amplification)
4) monitor 5 minutes, then re-evaluate
kevin: commands ready:
```
# increase burst capacity
rctl dedicated update-pool --id ded-acme-eu-1 --burst-capacity 3
# soft quota rule
rctl rate-limits create --customer acmepay --route /v1/generate --limit 200 --window 60
# feature flag off for customer
rctl feature-flags set --customer acmepay --flag ff.dynamic_system_prompts --value false
```
jess: I'll notify AcmePay SRE + support. Drafting asap: "We're applying temporary throttles and burst increase to stabilize latency; will follow up in 10m." tagging #acct-acmepay and support@acmepay
sre-bot: runbook step executed: increased ASG desired capacity +2 (op-id=op-98765)
deploy-bot: autoscale policy update accepted (policy-id=pol-3344)
maria: burst cap applied. Observability: queue depth dropping to 180, errors down to 1.1%.
oncall-lead: Good. Keep throttles minimal. If errors < 0.5% for 10min, lift route throttle and re-enable feature flag.
oliver: also recommend scheduling a Dedicated pool scale-up window for AcmePay traffic patterns; post-mortem item.
support-liaison: AcmePay notified at 08:23Z. They asked for ETA; told them ~15-20m while we stabilize. They're okay with temporary throttling as long as we follow up.
maria: monitoring: errors at 0.3% now, 95th latency 290ms. We'll keep the burst on for 30m, then revert if stable.
kevin: created incident ticket INC-2026-4321 and linked customer comms. Adding postmortem owners @oliver and @maria.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — error rate dropped under threshold. Action summary: burst +2, soft-rate-limit applied, feature flag toggled off for AcmePay. Incident to remain in watch mode for 1 hour.
jess: I'll send follow-up to AcmePay with actions and ask for any traffic pattern changes on their side.
maria: handing off to @oliver for watch window — I need to drop to have a quick break. @oliver please ack.
oliver: ack, taking over monitoring. Will notify if we need to scale further or roll back changes.
incident-bot: Incident watch started by oliver. If errors spike >1% again, pager will notify next oncall.
sre-bot: scheduled job: revert feature flag ff.dynamic_system_prompts for AcmePay in 30m unless cancelled (job-id=job-4421)
oliver: noted. setting a 30m timer to re-evaluate before revert.
maria: thanks team, good handoff. :thumbsup:
